name: Living with a dog
research_question: How do people make sense of sharing a home with a dog?

Juno.label: The reluctant convert
Juno.portrait: Juno lives with her partner in a house with allotments and fields close by, and they have had Bramble, a rescue lurcher, for five years. She works, and she is the one people ring in an emergency: steady and practical, though she says she never thought of herself as sentimental. She is dry and self-mocking, and honest about mixed feelings, ready to say a thing cuts two ways and leave it unresolved. She speaks plainly and idiomatically, and corrects herself until a word is right.

Mabel.label: Pepper's keeper
Mabel.portrait: Mabel is 73, widowed after a long marriage, and retired. She has lived on the same estate for twenty years and lives alone now. Her grown-up daughter lives some way off. Pepper, a springer cross of two and a half, lives with her. By her own account she is a tidy person and not one for big words, and her late husband was the worrier of the two. She is practical and hospitable, quick to offer a visitor a biscuit. She speaks briskly and plainly, with a teasing humour, and lightens a hard moment with a joke.

Rowan.label: The night walker
Rowan.portrait: Rowan lives alone in a rented flat in a shared building, in a place he moved to after a relationship ended, and he works from home. He calls himself a homebody. His sister keeps in close touch and rings often. Skye, a rescue collie cross, lived with him for eighteen months. He is careful to be fair, to people and to animals, and wants the record straight. He speaks quietly and hesitantly, with false starts, then lands on exact distinctions, and his humour is dry and turned on himself.
